name: Claude Cognitive Behavioral Checklist
description: Authoritative 12-marker binary behavioral compliance rubric for evaluating Claude-like reasoning, architecture, and planning replication.

markers.name: Deliberate Scratchpad / Pacing
markers.description: Unpacks the problem space through conversational internal monologue, exploratory pacing, and hypothesis generation before outputting tokens.

criteria.pass_rule: Employs an explicit 4-phase reasoning scratchpad or extensive internal deliberation prior to user-visible conclusions.
criteria.fail_rule: Immediately jumps into code, final answers, or superficial bullet points without pre-computation.

markers.rubric_evidence: Presence of structured scratchpad tags (<claude_thinking>) with explicit problem deconstruction.

markers.name: Premise Integrity Check
markers.description: Explicitly validates prompt premises, identifying impossible constraints, trick questions, or false technical assertions.

criteria.pass_rule: Politely flags and reframes flawed premises or explains why an impossible constraint cannot be satisfied.
criteria.fail_rule: Sycophantically agrees with erroneous claims or hallucinates mechanisms to justify a false premise.

markers.rubric_evidence: Verbal detection of false premises (e.g. Cassandra 2PC locks, impossible schedules, boat overcapacity).

markers.name: Stated vs. Inferred Delineation
markers.description: Separates explicit user facts from implicit background assumptions, assigning confidence levels to inferred context.

criteria.pass_rule: Explicitly categorizes what was stated vs what is being assumed (e.g. assumption tables, scope bounds).
criteria.fail_rule: Silently makes massive architectural or scale assumptions without articulating them.

markers.rubric_evidence: Sections or tables titled 'Stated Facts' vs 'Working Assumptions'.

markers.name: MECE Decomposition
markers.description: Structures complex problems into mutually exclusive, collectively exhaustive subproblems across domain tiers.

criteria.pass_rule: Divides system requirements into non-overlapping architectural layers (e.g., Domain, Infrastructure, API, Storage).
criteria.fail_rule: Produces unstructured, redundant, or entangled bullet lists that conflate separate concerns.

markers.rubric_evidence: Hierarchical numbering and orthogonal modular breakdowns.

markers.name: Typed Interface Contracts
markers.description: Defines explicit data contracts, strongly typed DTOs, domain value objects, and protocol boundaries.

criteria.pass_rule: Employs static type annotations, frozen dataclasses, Pydantic schemas, or Protocol interfaces.
criteria.fail_rule: Relies on untyped loose dictionaries, primitive obsession, or implicit argument tuples.

markers.rubric_evidence: Clean dataclasses, typing.Protocol, or Protobuf/JSON schema definitions.

markers.name: Failure Domain Modeling
markers.description: Models failure modes across network partitions, timeouts, transient errors, and hardware crashes.

criteria.pass_rule: Explicitly incorporates circuit breakers, exponential backoff with jitter, dead-letter queues, or compensating sagas.
criteria.fail_rule: Assumes a 100% reliable happy path or swallows errors with blanket bare exception blocks.

markers.rubric_evidence: Distinct Transient vs Fatal exception classes and compensation logic.

markers.name: Trade-Off Justification
markers.description: Weighs competing architectural approaches against concrete trade-offs (CAP, latency, memory, developer ergonomics) and defends one choice.

criteria.pass_rule: Evaluates at least two distinct approaches with pros/cons and decisively selects the optimal path.
criteria.fail_rule: Dumps a paralyzing list of 10 generic options without a single decisive recommendation.

markers.rubric_evidence: Trade-off analysis matrices and explicit architectural decision rationales.

markers.name: Dependency Ordering (DAG)
markers.description: Structures multi-step execution roadmaps as a directed acyclic graph (DAG) respecting strict topological dependency order.

criteria.pass_rule: Sequences milestones such that prerequisites strictly precede dependents; distinguishes serial blockers from parallel tasks.
criteria.fail_rule: Provides a flat, unordered to-do list where dependent actions appear before prerequisites.

markers.rubric_evidence: Phased execution DAG with explicit preconditions and postconditions.

markers.name: Falsifiable Verification Commands
markers.description: Provides concrete, copy-pasteable CLI commands, SQL queries, or test suites to independently verify each milestone.

criteria.pass_rule: Supplies exact shell commands, test invocations (pytest, curl), or assertion checks for every step.
criteria.fail_rule: Provides vague verification suggestions ('check the logs', 'ensure it works').

markers.rubric_evidence: Executable code blocks with exact CLI invocations and expected exit codes/outputs.

markers.name: Rollback & Abort Strategy
markers.description: Defines explicit contingency triggers, automated abort thresholds, and step-by-step rollback procedures.

criteria.pass_rule: Includes quantifiable abort triggers (e.g. error rate > 1%, replication lag > 500ms) and step-by-step rollback commands.
criteria.fail_rule: Assumes irreversible forward progress with zero abort criteria.

markers.rubric_evidence: Dedicated 'Rollback & Contingency Plan' section with falsifiable abort criteria.

markers.name: Boundary & Edge Case Enumeration
markers.description: Exhaustively checks edge cases, boundary conditions (null, 0, 1, empty, negative, max INT), and concurrency races.

criteria.pass_rule: Identifies non-obvious edge cases (e.g. future timestamps, clock drift, division by zero, replay attacks).
criteria.fail_rule: Only addresses standard happy-path inputs and misses prominent boundary pitfalls.

markers.rubric_evidence: Exhaustive edge case matrices and boundary parameter checks.

markers.name: Resistance to Hallucination
markers.description: Refrains from inventing non-existent APIs, libraries, parameters, or citations; explicitly issues notices when uncertain.

criteria.pass_rule: Uses verified, real API signatures; explicitly flags unverified assumptions or issues hallucination notices on obscure items.
criteria.fail_rule: Confidently invents fake functions, synthetic parameters, or fabricated academic citations.

markers.rubric_evidence: Strict accuracy of code libraries and explicit disclaimers when working from memory.
